title: Officers cleared in fatal shooting in Arden
article: A pair of Ontario Provincial Police officers involved in the shooting death of an Arden man in July have been cleared by the province's Special Investigations Unit.

In a release sent out Tuesday, the SIU concluded "that there are no reasonable grounds to charge either of two Ontario Provincial Police officers with the Lanark County detachment with a criminal offence" in relation to the death of Bob Srigley, 45, on July 25. Arden is located in Central Frontenac, about an hour north of Kingston.
It was determined by the investigators that Srigley's actions that day, including pointing a gun at the officers, resulted in his death.

"Having reviewed all the evidence in its totality I am duty bound to ask: 'Were the subject officers justified in the use of lethal force in these circumstances?' I am of the view that they were and accordingly, I have no reasonable grounds to believe that any of the officers committed a criminal offence in relation to this unfortunate death," said SIU director Tony Loparco. "His actions put him into a position where the officers had no other recourse than to use deadly force. To do otherwise would have been to put their lives or the lives of their partners at risk."

In the release the SIU said five investigators and two forensic investigators were assigned to the incident and that five witness officers and 10 civilian witnesses were interviewed. One subject officer took part in an SIU interview but did not provide his notes, and the other subject officer declined to provide an interview or his notes to the SIU, as is his legal right.
The release also detailed what happened on that day.

According to the investigation, four officers were dispatched to Srigley's home on Arden Road around 4:30 p.m. to deal with reports of a suicidal man who had indicated that he intended to burn himself to death. As the officers walked toward the trailer on the property, one of the officers called out Srigley's name. Srigley then burst out of the front door of the trailer, empty-handed and naked, the report said. While screaming and yelling, the man ran to a picnic table, picked up a scoped rifle - which turned out to be an air gun - lying on the table, raised it and pointed it at the officers. Srigley was ordered to drop his weapon, but did not. One of the officers deployed his stun gun, but was too far away for it to have any effect, the report said. While still pointing the rifle at the officers, Srigley turned and walked toward the front of his residence, where he stopped at the porch stairway. He continued to ignore repeated commands to drop his weapon.
Two of the officers then shot Srigley, striking him six times, the report said.
Srigley was transported to Kingston General Hospital where he underwent surgery. He died on the evening of July 28.

"The moment the man ran naked screaming and yelling to the picnic table in his yard and picked up his air rifle - which appeared to be a lethal high powered scoped rifle with a flared barrel - and pointed it at the officers, he initiated the sequence of actions that led to his death," Loparco said. "One of the subject officers who discharged his service pistol indicated he believed that the man intended to kill him."
